summary: Stanley Abe specializes in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Duke University (attested in 1995 and 2004).

Stanley Insler (1937–2019) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Columbia University, the University of Tübingen, and Yale University, working under Paul Thieme, and taught at Yale from circa 1964 to 2012.

Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah (1929–2014) worked in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Peradeniya and Cornell University, later teaching at Peradeniya (1955–1960), Cambridge (1963–1973), Chicago (1973–1976), and Harvard (1976–2001).

Stanley Lombardo is a scholar of linguistics and philosophy. He studied at Loyola University New Orleans, Tulane University, and the University of Texas at Austin, and held a post at the University of Kansas from circa 1976 to 2014.

Stanley Weinstein (1929–2017) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Komazawa, Tokyo, and Harvard Universities, and held faculty appointments at Komazawa, SOAS University of London, and Yale University.

Stanley Wolpert (1927–2019) was an Indologist and historian. He studied at the City College of New York and the University of Pennsylvania, and spent his career at the University of California, Los Angeles from 1959 until 2002.
Stefan Anacker (1939–2021) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from circa 1964 to 1970 under Alex Wayman.

Stefan Baums is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He completed his dissertation at the University of Washington (2001–2009) and held posts at the University of Copenhagen, Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich, and Bavarian Academy of Sciences.

Stefan Larsson specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Stockholm University under Per-Arne Berglie and Erik af Edholm, and was a postdoctoral fellow at the University of California, Berkeley in 2012.

Stefan Mario Maul is a historian and linguist. He studied at the University of Göttingen and Free University of Berlin, where he also worked, before becoming Ordinarius for Assyriology at Heidelberg University in 1995.

Stefania Travagnin specializes in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She held an assistant professorship at the University of Groningen from circa 2013 to 2020 and joined SOAS University of London in 2020.

Stefano Zacchetti (1968–2020) was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He studied at Ca' Foscari University, Sichuan University, and Leiden University, later holding posts at Soka University, Ca' Foscari, and as Yehan Numata Professor at Oxford (2012–2020).

Steffen Döll is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Munich and Kyoto University, later working as an assistant at Munich before becoming Numata Professor of Japanese Buddhism at the University of Hamburg in 2015.

Stella Kramrisch (1896–1993) was an Indologist and art historian who studied at the University of Vienna. She taught at Visva-Bharati University, the University of Calcutta, the University of Pennsylvania, and New York University, also curating at the Philadelphia Museum of Art.

Sten Konow (1867–1948) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Oslo and the University of Halle under Richard Pischel, later holding posts at Oslo, the Archaeological Survey of India, and the University of Hamburg.
Stephan Beyer specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Richard Hugh Robinson and served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested in 1977).
Stephan Marcus Salzberg specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at the University of British Columbia (attested 1983) under Yoshitaka Iriya, Shoko Kanaoka, and Daniel L. Overmyer.

Stephanie Kaza specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. She completed degrees at Oberlin College, Stanford University, UC Santa Cruz, and Starr King School for the Ministry, and served on the faculty of the University of Vermont from 1991 to 2015.
Stephanie Roemer is a scholar of Tibetology who conducted doctoral research under supervisors Eberhard Sandschneider and Toni Huber.

Stephanie W. Jamison is an Indologist and linguist. She completed doctoral studies at Yale University under Stanley Insler and Warren Cowgill, later holding posts at Harvard University and the University of California, Los Angeles (appointed professor circa 2002).
